chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Nawfalī, who said:

Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj said to me that Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام wrote to him: “O Muḥammad, put your affairs together and take your precaution.” He said: “So I was putting my affairs together, and I did not know what he had written to me, until a messenger came to me, carried me away from Miṣr in fetters, seized everything I owned, and I remained in prison for eight years.”

Then a letter came to me from him in the prison, in which was: “O Muḥammad, do not reside in the district of the western side.” So I read the letter and said: “He writes this to me while I am in prison? Indeed, this is astonishing.” Then it was not long before I was released, and all praise is due to Allah.

He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj wrote to him asking him about his estates, so he wrote to him: “They will soon be returned to you, and what harm is there to you if they are not returned to you?” Then when Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj went to al-ʿAskar, an order was written for the return of his estates, but he died before that.

He said: Aḥmad ibn al-Khaḍīb wrote to Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj asking him about going out to al-ʿAskar. So he wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام seeking his counsel, and he wrote to him: “Go out, for in it will be your relief, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.” So he went out, and he did not remain long except a little while until he died.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam عليه السلام referred to in the report
key_terms.أَجْمِعْ أَمْرَكَ: Put your affairs in order and prepare carefully
key_terms.خُذْ حِذْرَكَ: Take precaution and be on guard

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the guidance of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام to Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj during imprisonment and hardship?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates reports concerning Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj and the correspondence of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, including warnings, foreknowledge of imprisonment and release, and mention of his estates and eventual death. It reflects the Imam’s guidance during times of hardship and political pressure, and records events connected to al-ʿAskar and those associated with him.
